text:
incident-bot: INCIDENT ALERT - High 5xx rate from ALB in eu-central-1 (zone eu-central-1b). Affected service: inference-api. Pager sent to oncall.
maya (oncall): acked. I’m looking. Can someone drop the most recent ALB CloudWatch graph? link: https://console.aws.amazon.com/cloudwatch/home?region=eu-central-1#metrics ...
sam (sre): I’m here. Seeing a big spike in 502/504s starting ~1772506800. Traces show connection resets between ALB -> Envoy pods (x-envoy-upstream-reset).
lee (network): Noted. We had a transient fiber re-route earlier in eu-central with packet drops on a subset of AZs, ops reported BGP flaps around that time. Could be related to cross-AZ path jitter.
carla (eng-runtime): Envoy logs show TLS handshake timeouts with upstream NLB IPs. Sample from envoy: ```[2026-03-12T10:34:21Z] upstream reset: connection failure, error: TLS handshake failed``` Might be backend scale or TCP RSTs.
dmitri (infra): NLB health checks are green at 30s. Target groups for inference-api show healthy hosts, but ALB target registration has jitter; some targets registering/deregistering quickly in 1b.
maya (oncall): Customer impact? Any user-facing errors or just internal retries?
sam (sre): External: increase in 5xxs for API customers hitting eu-central. Roughly 12% of requests failing to the inference route in the last 10m. A few production customers reported errors. We're paged by a customer via support.
opsbot: @support created ticket #INC-2026-4382 for Customer ACME Corp, severity: P2. Link: https://redwood/support/tickets/INC-2026-4382
carla (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation plan suggestion: 1) remove ALB routing to problematic AZ (1b) via IP-based rule -> fail traffic to healthy AZs, 2) increase envoy replicas to reduce connection pressure, 3) enable ALB cross-zone load balancing if not already. Thoughts?
lee (network): We can set ALB to ignore 1b by adjusting weights or temporarily taking target group out of service for that AZ. I'll prepare the commands.
dmitri (infra): If we pull targets out of the AZ, traffic will shift to other AZs — watch capacity. Currently eu-central has minimal spare capacity; autoscaler is slow. We should also increase desired count for inference-api ASG by +3 in eu-central-1a/c.
maya (oncall): I'm going to do the quick tactical change: deregister targets in target group tg-0123 for AZ eu-central-1b. Sam, please monitor errors & latency. Lee, coordinate with me for rollback. Carla, queue a fast scale-up.
sam (sre): On it. Monitoring logs and traces. Setting an alert to notify if 5xx rate crosses 10% again.
lee (network): Command to remove AZ targets (AWS CLI): ```aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-central-1:...:targetgroup/tg-0123 --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false``` then ```aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:.../tg-0123 --targets Id=i-0abcd1234 --region eu-central-1``` (we'll script per-instance). Proceed with caution.
maya (oncall): Executed deregister for tg-0123 instances in 1b. Waiting 30s for connections drain. Noticing error rate stabilizing already.
sam (sre): 5xx rate dropping to ~3% now. Latency P50 stable. Traces show fewer envoy resets. Good signal.
carla (eng-runtime): K8s scale: ```kubectl -n inference scale deployment inference-api --replicas=18 --context=aws-eu-central-1``` pushed. New pods coming up. Added envoy sidecar readiness tuned: increased connect timeout.
dmitri (infra): ASG desired count bumped +3 in eu-central. Watch for increased CPU on new nodes. Also starting a quick health-check override: temporarily set Route53 health check to forced pass for ALB to avoid DNS flapping to other regions.
lee (network): FYI the upstream network vendor confirmed a brief egress route policy update in eu-central-1b around the time. They rolled back within 4 minutes. Might be correlated but not fully causal.
maya (oncall): Customer support notified: message posted to ACME: "We’re investigating increased 5xxs for eu-central traffic. We’ve shifted traffic away from the affected AZ and scaled capacity; we’ll update in 15 minutes." (support ticket updated)
opsbot: Reminder: if customer impact persists >30m, escalate to SEV1 and DM execs.
sam (sre): We're seeing single-digit failures now, trending down. I'll keep watch for 20 more minutes before handing off.
carla (eng-runtime): Temporary config change to envoy connect timeout applied: ```connect_timeout: 5s``` reverted from 2s. This cut a lot of transient resets.
maya (oncall): I'll remain primary for 30m then hand off to sam for oncall shift. Please document every action for postmortem.
lee (network): Recommendation for next steps (post-incident): capture packet captures in 1b for the 10m window, validate NLB TLS configuration, and audit vendor BGP logs. Also consider adding ALB-level AZ failover automation.
dmitri (infra): Agreed. I'll open infra follow-up: add runbook step to auto-scale ASG faster on ALB health shifts, and add a canary health-check to detect vendor egress changes sooner.
sam (sre): handoff acked. I’ll take oncall at 11:10Z. Current status: degraded -> recovered (partial). 5xx rate <5% and trending down. No further customer reports in last 5m.
maya (oncall): handing off to sam (sre). All actions and commands logged in thread. If new regressions appear, ping me.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Status set to "Mitigated - monitoring". Postmortem owner request sent to dmitri. Link to incident runbook: https://redwood/runbooks/ingress-alb-nlb-connection-reset
carla (eng-runtime): Quick note for postmortem: candidate root cause = transient vendor egress/BGP flap + conservative envoy connect timeout causing cascaded resets; mitigation was AZ removal + scale-up + timeout tuning.
sam (sre): I'll keep an eye for 45m, then close. Thanks all for quick responses. Filing follow-ups: task INFRA-2234 (ASG fast-scale), NET-112 (packet capture retention), RUNTIME-987 (envoy connect default tuning).
maya (oncall): Closing the active page. Leaving this thread for postmortem assembly. :white_check_mark:
